title: Taxes in Simple Words
subtitle: Navigating STCG, LTCG, TDS, and slab rates across Indian securities
summary: A simplified plain-language overview of how profits, dividends, and interest payouts are taxed across stocks, REITs, InvITs, and bonds following recent Finance Act changes.

sources.name: Income Tax Department of India (Finance Act 2024 provisions)
Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT) Circulars

disclaimer: Educational information only. Not investment advice. TradeOne is not a SEBI-registered investment adviser. Rules, taxes and yields change; verify with official sources.

sections.title: How Securities Taxation Works in India
sections.content: Every rupee earned from financial securities falls into one of two fundamental buckets: Capital Gains (profits when you sell an asset for more than you paid) or Periodic Income (dividends, interest, rental distributions). The tax treatment differs significantly between these two buckets.
sections.analogy: Think of periodic income like apples picked from your orchard each month (taxed as regular income at your tax slab), while selling the entire orchard land for a profit is a capital gain (taxed at special capital gain rates depending on how long you owned it).

sections.title: Capital Gains: The 12-Month Rule
sections.content: For listed Indian securities (Stocks, Equity ETFs, REITs, InvITs, and listed bonds):
points: Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG): If you hold the listed asset for 12 months or less before selling. For listed equities and REIT/InvIT units, STCG is taxed at 20% (post Finance Act 2024). For unlisted debt or short-term bonds, gains are taxed at your income slab.

Long-Term Capital Gains (LTCG): If you hold the listed asset for more than 12 months. For listed equities and REIT/InvIT units, LTCG is taxed at 12.5% on cumulative gains exceeding ₹1.25 lakh in a financial year. For listed debt bonds, LTCG is 12.5% without indexation benefit.

sections.title: Understanding Periodic Cash Flow Taxation
sections.content: Tax treatment on cash that enters your bank account before you sell:
points: Dividends from Stocks: Added to your gross total income and taxed at your personal slab rate (TDS applies at 10% if dividend exceeds ₹5,000 from a single company).
Bond Coupon Interest: Added to total income and taxed at slab rate.
REIT & InvIT Distributions: Split into interest (slab rate), dividend (exempt if SPV under 115BAA, else slab rate), and repayment of capital (subject to Section 56(2)(xii) rules).

sections.title: Special Tax-Exempt Instruments
sections.content: Certain debt and precious metal securities offer specialized tax benefits:
points: Sovereign Gold Bonds (SGB): 100% exempt from capital gains tax upon redemption through RBI at 8-year maturity for individuals under Section 47(viic).
Tax-Free Infrastructure Bonds: Bonds issued earlier by NHAI, REC, PFC, and IRFC provide 100% tax-free coupon interest under Section 10(15)(iv)(h).

sections.title: Worked Example: Capital Gains Calculation
sections.content: Suppose an investor sells listed REIT units after 18 months, realizing a profit of ₹1,75,000, and has no other capital gains.
details: LTCG tax payable: 12.5% of ₹50,000 = ₹6,250 (plus applicable 4% health & education cess).

sections.title: TDS and Advance Tax Readiness
sections.content: Points to keep in mind when filing ITR:
points: Always verify Form 26AS and AIS (Annual Information Statement) before filing returns. High-value transactions and bond TDS are automatically matched by the IT Department.
Submit Form 15G (for individuals below 60) or Form 15H (for senior citizens) to your broker/DP if your total taxable income is below the exemption threshold to avoid TDS deduction.

items.myth: All income from government bonds is tax-free.
items.fact: Regular semi-annual interest from standard G-Secs is fully taxable at your income tax slab rate. Only designated tax-free PSU bonds or SGB maturity capital gains are exempt.

items.myth: Indexation benefit is still available on all debt bonds.
items.fact: Recent Finance Acts have removed indexation benefits across listed and unlisted debt investments; listed bonds are now subject to a flat 12.5% LTCG rate without indexation.

terms.definition: Short-Term Capital Gain - profit from selling an asset held for a short period (12 months or less for listed securities).
Long-Term Capital Gain - profit from selling an asset held for a longer duration.
Tax Deducted at Source - tax collected upfront by the payer and credited to your PAN with the tax department.
